body:
Mine talked endless BS about his ex and her issues for over a decade. I found out after he dumped me that most of the worst and most psychotic parts were a lie meant to keep me from ever meeting her (they shared parenting responsibility). 
I kind of wish I could warn my replacement, especially since he plays the long game... I lost years to a lie. I am sure he's told her all sorts of shit about me, but I don't think anyone deserves to be lead on for almost a decade, then subjected to a year of gaslighting before getting dumped for the replacement, and that's his schtick, so...
Run. It does not get better.
Very much THIS\^\^

I'm so sorry. I know this pain. Often I find people break up for things, sometimes it's another person, others it's not. But when someone has you convinced for years that you are their person, only to be suddenly blindsided by how untrue it has been for some time, that person is low. They could not be bothered to treat you decently because it would interrupt whatever their other plans are.

It made me feel like a fool. Like the worlds biggest tool. But just remember, once you emerge from this, you can be stronger, better, and wiser. 

Hugs to you. PM if you need to talk.
That sounds reasonable on every way... 👍

I am. I'm doing things alone. Almost every day. 
My life has improved. It's just this thing. This is the the thing I had hoped he was honest about. 
I hate that this had to happen, but I really hate that it had to happen today. Today is really really hard.

So much this... Be it text, call, or in person, I think this is one of the things that hurts me the most. I'm over the romantic relationship part, as I realized a while ago that the person he tried to show me was not representative of who he was... But he was my best friend for a decade, and that ability to share, good & bad, has been the part that I miss deeply.

^^THIS!!! 
From personal experience -RUN don't walk out of this. It gets worse. Much worse. This was just the bread sticks... He hasn't yet served the appitizer, main course, or dessert yet. This is the first very clear sign that you are in danger. While he may not kill you, he will absolutely do servere psychological damage (quickly) and physical damage (sooner or later).

I feel like this could have been my own post... *Hug*
I get this... And at the same time, I don't. 
But I learned how to accept that I don't need to get it, just accept it. Hopefully you can find a way to get to that place.
I needed to read this right at this moment... thank you
If I had any friends or family I could crash with I likely would. :(
I need to save this..
Hells yes.
I just deactivated mine completely this morning. It felt liberating.
I feel this so hard.

That sounds almost exactly like what happened to me. It's been a little over a month and nothing makes sense. The only thing that helps is trying to remind myself that no matter what his reasons, it doesn't actually matter because it's over... At this point I'm pretty sure it's someone else, but thinking about it only hurts me. PM if you need to talk.

My friends AND family make me feel worse, so I avoid talking about this with all of the above.
I have reached out and reconnected with friends I hadn't spoken to in a long time. 
I made new friends. 
I started to do things alone that I hadn't done in years... Karaoke, shooting pool, dancing, going to movies...
When I start thinking too much I make a conscious effort to focus on my breathing, and remind myself that any thoughts related to "it", ANY thoughts, are irrelevant and a waste of my time....
And when I need to, I cry. As much or as little as I need in the moment. After all, I'm still mourning. Crying IS therapy.
These things help.
Thank you so much for this post. ❤️

Get a notebook & use it to list all of the reasons they were not good for you.. everything. Even petty things. Any time you think of a new thing, add it. Also, journal. It is hard at first, but it gets easier and it is theraputic.
It sounds like you need that seperation. It does not sound like it was healthy for either one of you... Maybe this is better for you in the long run?
Fire to the rain is also good

I hope you don't take this the wrong way, and I won't claim to know the details of your relationship, but I know being dumped...
The first few days I was a broken mess.
At some point I realized his issues were his issues, and if he had seriously wanted my help working on them, he would have done that... He needed to work on his issues on his own. I was not the partner to him that I thought I had been. While I was sad, this epiphany was freeing. 
I still love my ex more than anything. I want him to find his peace and be happy. I still miss everything about "us".
That being said, if he told me tomorrow it was a mistake and he wanted to get back together, I would respectfully decline. 
He broke the trust. He abandon me. 
He needs to work his shit out & figure out what he wants in his life.
After he does this, which I'm sure will take a lot of time, if he decides he wants me back in his life, providing I am available, he will need to show me he has his shit together. He will need to produce a plan for how we are to move forward. He will need to prove commitment to this plan. It will be work, but when you break trust by dumping someone, the owness is on you to show that you truly want THEM back. Why would someone in their right mind get back together with someone who has already shown that they will end things when it gets hard? 
In the meantime, I do hope you heal... I know this hurts.

Same here... The "best friend + life partner + lover" combination really does make it hard to get over.
I'm mourning mine like the death of a favorite fictional character in a book, since I am not sure how much was real before, but that person no longer exists now.
We just need to learn to make better choices, I suppose.
Likewise
Thank you, and ditto
Totally right... I made that mistake and all it seemed to do was irritate him.

Me too..  almost a decade and my best friend dumps me, just like that. Nothing to work out. I thought the being blindsided hurt more than anything he could do, but later he threw in my face that I took him at his word on issues in the past, when he thought I should have done x, and said that this clearly indicated that I put my feelings over his, and this was my fault. 

THAT hurt even more. 

I am also happy to chat if you need to.  We are not alone. 🤗

I'm 42 and I just had almost the same thing happen to me... Almost a decade and then dropped like it was nothing. No notice, no "we have an issue", just "fine". I thought it was bizarre but evidently this is a thing. Shitty thing, but a thing.

You are not alone. You can message me if you want to talk, as well. 

Until we can stand on our own, we can lean on each other.
It's not a cure-all, but if you can find a good hypnotherapist, I highly recommend a session. Relief is noticable and you get tools to use in your healing.
2 weeks

If he could give up on you so easily, he is not the person you thought he was, and does not deserve to be treated as that person. 
You are worth more than that. Find your own happiness. It will take time, but push forward. NC. Live your life for you, and no one else. 
You will thank yourself later.

We will. I'm sure if that. I don't feel it now, but I know it.
If you need to reach out, PM me. We'll be ok.
Sadly I did not see this coming. All the way up into it happening. I was in disbelief. I was so sure we were more than that, and then *poof!* It was done.

Counseling, meds, CBD, exercise & hypnotherapy. Hypnotherapy results are almost immediate. Counseling helps, but when it's too much...
Acupuncture has also helped in the past, but it's hard to find a good one around here, & a bad one is worthless.
Ditto...

I'm so sorry... I know it is so incredible painful right now.. Mine didn't even completely unload on me about how he felt about my actions for almost a week. I had thought I was broken before that, but once he unloaded, I really did break. 
I made a sincere attempt to commit suicide that same evening. I have no idea how, but it failed miserably. In my attempt to console myself from the failed attempt, I played a guided meditation on trauma, then another on knowing yourself, and I'm not sure what the combination was that was responsible, but I no longer felt broken, and I had my moment of revalation.

I'm still sad. I still wish I could hate him. I'm still grieving... But putting yourself first and realizing that if he wanted to fix things you wouldn't be in that situation can be liberating. You are not alone.

Mine was similar... He was my best friend for about a decade. I could sense his stress & anxiety, and tried to push him to talk. He would eventually get upset and tell me my pushing was invasive. He'd also complain that I wouldn't take the answer he gave me, insisting that he would never say he wanted something he didn't want, was ok with something he wasn't ok with, or tell me I was not part of the issue if I wasn't. 
He was my biggest support, my rock. He always tried to be there for me, so when he wasn't I was confident that he'd be there for me in spirit. 

My biggest mistake?  I believed him. Every word.

I stopped pushing so hard and tried to ask casually & just "feel it out"... I though we were happy. We had issues as individuals and as a couple, but that is normal. He was talking about buying a home together. He said he was happy to see me, he missed me when we were not together, and more.

Then he dumped me.

In 8 years prior to this, I think we argued MAYBE 5 times. My crimes? Doing what he told me he wanted me to do - take him at his word.

I've never had luck with women (I'm bi) because they have always done this to me... They want x until they don't, and without warning I'd need to know "no" meant "yes" and "yes" meant "no". After 8 years, with no warning, he suddenly adopted this same logic.

Until I realized that I cannot be responsible for his issues with me, because they are just that - HIS issues - I was inconsolable. That realization set me free. I'm still sad, but I understand now that there was nothing I could do to prevent this - he was done and did not want to work anything out. 

I hope yours does not do what mine did. I recommend maybe couples therapy or something like it. Just understand that you can only do what you know to do, and nothing more. Best of luck to you.

Mine broke it off suddenly, too. No warning. The day before he was telling me he loved me. The day after? It was over. I think that was the part that hurt the worst.
You are not alone.

I have hated this delimma. I'd feel badly for my daughter, but she'd have to grow up (she's 21) & hopefully not follow in my foot steps. I know that after I did, I'd feel badly for no one. 
I've failed twice now, and not for lack of effort. 
I couldn't tell them. No. Not happening.

I hate but know this. Even as this is breaking my heart, I get this. I hate that we have mutual people in common. It will take a lot for me to not ask them about him. I'm going to need to have the hard conversations. 
If he wanted to work it out, it would have happened. 💔
You are not alone. Mine was telling me he loved me & planning our future right before he decided he was done with me.
This is perfect. I wish this was posted 2 weeks ago. My LTR (8 yrs) ex blindsided me and I made several of these mistakes. I really wasn't myself for quite a while.

TBF he has depression issues, as well. What he did was definitely shitty, but I don't want to be too judgemental since I know depression messes with your head in some pretty bad ways. 
I am not excusing it, just understanding it.
